turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on back, Ms. Keller. I'm gonna grab a blood pressure real quick before Dr. Alvarez sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh thank you. Sorry if my hands are cold, that waiting room vent blows right on the chair, I was gonna mention it to somebody.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Yeah it's always freezing out there. Arm relaxed. Okay, one thirty two over eighty four, and your pulse is seventy eight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy eight, is that fast? I had a large coffee with cream, which is probably dumb given why I'm here.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor can sort that out. Have a seat on the table, she'll be right in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Alvarez. What brought you in today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this pain. Right up under my ribs, the right side. It shows up after I eat something fatty.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. How long does an episode last?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Hours. Not minutes. Like I'll have fried chicken and an hour later it starts, and it can go four, five hours, last Saturday I was up till midnight with it.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the character of it, sharp, crampy, burning?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): More dull and heavy, like a brick. Sometimes it sneaks around to my back, the right shoulder blade. And umm one time I threw up.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Just the once?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah just once, couple weeks ago, after ribs from that place on Main. I felt better after, which was disgusting, and my husband was not impressed. We were supposed to watch a movie.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever or chills with these episodes?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I checked with the thermometer, it was normal.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bowels okay? Any diarrhea, constipation, blood in the stool?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, all normal. Sorry, that's a lot of movie detail you didn't ask for.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're fine. Any yellow color in the eyes or the skin, or urine looking like tea?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of that. My coworker had yellow eyes from hepatitis and I got paranoid and checked the mirror. Nothing there.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did this whole thing start? Can you date the first time?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm honestly I can't tell you. Somewhere in the last few months. Could've been March, could've been May, err, I keep thinking I'll remember and I don't.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, we'll leave the start date fuzzy. What are you taking for it?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Tums. I chew two tablets when it kicks in, takes the edge off, doesn't kill it. I was on omeprozole, twenty milligrams every morning, they gave it last year, but I stopped it in March, wasn't doing much and the copay was silly.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the omeprazole is done, and you're just on the Tums now.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. The pharmacist talked about a stronger one, but I never even picked it up, so I never took that.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thinking out loud, pain after fat that lasts for hours up on the right, plus that one vomit, that pattern is the gallbladder squeezing against a stone. I'd call it biliary colic for now. An ulcer can sit in the upper belly too, and I wouldn't fully rule that out, but the fatty meal trigger fits stones better. Anyone in the family with gallbladder trouble?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh my mother had her gallbladder taken out. She was fine after, back to her garden and everything. I was gonna say the rest of the family if you want it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah, go ahead, anyone else?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar. That's Linda, she lives in Ohio, and she calls me every Sunday which is sweet but long. Dad passed about ten years back.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Got it. Tell me about work, your day, food, exercise, alcohol.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a bookkeeper at a little firm downtown, umm about forty hours a week, and I stay late some Thursdays for payroll. Diet is honestly bad, lots of takeout, fried stuff, burgers, and I walk the dog most evenings, like twenty minutes around the block. Wine, one glass with dinner most nights, and I don't smoke, never have. Oh and the dog is a beagle mix, he eats better than I do, which is sad.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): The beagle's winning. Lie back and let me feel your belly.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Uh, tell me if I should breathe or not, I always forget.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Just breathe normal. Tender right under the ribs here when I press. No guarding. The rest of the belly is soft.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah that's the spot. Ow, a little. Sorry.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): I want a liver panel, a lipase, and an ultrasound of the gallbladder. I'll put those orders in today. Not maybe, we're doing them.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Ultrasound like the jelly thing? My mom said hers didn't hurt.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Exactly, no pain, they just look. Avoid the fried meals till we know, and Tums is fine to keep using as you have been. If you get a fever, you turn yellow, or the pain won't quit, that's the ER, don't wait on me.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. So like two weeks, or what?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in about two weeks, after the ultrasound, and we'll go over the results. Front desk will book that and the scan.
[SEG0041] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book the ultrasound and the follow up on your way out, Ms. Keller.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Perfect. Do I need to fast for the blood?
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): For the ultrasound yes, nothing to eat for about six hours before. The bloodwork you can do today, no need to fast for what I'm ordering.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I'll skip the burger on the way home. Probably.

spec.situation: Woman with right-upper stomach pain after fatty meals, lasting hours, once with vomiting; takes antacid; mother had gallbladder surgery; blood tests and ultrasound planned.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Pain details supported, but certainty is not uncertain; patient describes it definitively.

omissions.text: Right upper abdominal pain is described as dull/heavy 'like a brick' and sometimes radiates to the back/right shoulder blade.
Patient reported bowel movements are normal.
Patient stopped omeprazole in March because it was not doing much and the copay was expensive.
Patient reported she never picked up or took the stronger medication the pharmacist mentioned.
Follow-up is specifically to occur after the ultrasound to review results, and front desk/clinical staff will book both the scan and follow-up.
Bloodwork can be done today and does not require fasting.
